notes: ares (Super Nintendo, Mega Drive, Mega CD, 32X): pkgforge-dev's sharun repackaging of ares v148 (hiro GTK frontend). Replaces Snes9x (2026-10-07), whose GTK frontend runs its whole exit inside its SIGTERM handler and crashes on every OpenGamepadUI Exit.

system_args: ares must be told the system (--system takes ares's own names; a .bin or .cue alone is ambiguous). Paths/Saves is set per launch with --setting (not saved to settings.bml): saves AND states go to ~/saves/<system>/<ares system name>/ (ares appends its system name; it has no separate state folder, so ~/states/<system> stays empty). Without it ares writes them next to the ROM.

--pseudofullscreen, never --fullscreen: ares's GLX fullscreen renders at the monitor's size and offset into a window gamescope never resizes (763x576 on a 1920x1080 output: picture off-centre, right and bottom cropped; HW 2026-10-07, Pocket Max). Pseudo fullscreen makes the GTK window itself fullscreen, which gamescope honours.
--kiosk: minimal UI, no file prompts, an error instead of a dialog (a missing Mega CD BIOS ends the launch with a message).

Exit: ares installs no signal handler, so OpenGamepadUI's Exit (SIGTERM) ends it at once: no crash, no final save. Battery saves are flushed every 30 s (General/AutoSaveMemory, on by default), so only the last 30 s after an in-game save are at risk. Its Quit hotkey binds one button only (no Select + Start): left unbound, OGUI's Exit is the way out.

Mega CD BIOS: ares finds firmware only through its GUI Scan button, so settings.bml names the files: ~/bios/segacd/bios_CD_U.bin, bios_CD_E.bin, bios_CD_J.bin (the names RetroArch's Genesis Plus GX uses); ares checks their sha256. The 32X and the Mega Drive need none.
gui_args: ares's own window (touch screen; no pad-driven UI).
